artifacts.name: Siri-for-Windows-Native-exe
artifacts.description: ZIP containing Siri-for-Windows.exe: unsigned, native C#/WPF, self-contained .NET 8 x64, single-file. No Electron, Chromium, WebView, Python or Node runtime. Requires Ollama with a local model for AI. Wake requires opt-in and installed English Windows speech recognition; running app only.

artifacts.name: Siri-Android-debug-apk
artifacts.description: ZIP containing the separately built Android debug HTTPS companion APK (v2.1). Not a native WPF client or on-device model. Requires separately hosted trusted HTTPS companion web UI; native WPF EXE does not host its backend.

validation: 34 companion/domain tests passed in Windows CI.

Native domain tests passed: wake intent/revocation, threshold/cooldown, cent arithmetic, payment validation, allowlisted task plans, case-insensitive exclusions, excluded-history filtering, cloud/remote model metadata.
Actual self-contained native EXE published and verified without required loose DLLs.
Actual WPF EXE launched in Windows CI; accessible composer found, wake activation visibly off; second launch exited successfully after activation handoff.
limitations: Real microphone recognition, accessibility fields, classic Outlook, browser history locks, model inference, screenshots and Android hardware need real-device verification. CI did not enable a microphone or send a real inference request.
Native feature parity is not complete: legacy tags, word-level writing diffs and Markdown previews are not all ported. Native and legacy stores are separate.
Native wake listens only after explicit per-session opt-in while the app runs; no closed-app background service.
GitHub sign-in/extraction and artifact retention apply. SHA-256 values identify artifact ZIP archives, not the inner EXE/APK.
localDownload: Sandbox outbound policy blocks GitHub artifact blob-storage redirects; actual compiled binaries are available at the hosted artifact URLs, not copied into this checkout.
